explanation: Use Pascal’s recurrence C(n,k)=C(n−1,k)+C(n−1,k−1), memoizing repeated subproblems. Choosing zero or all items has exactly one outcome.
timeComplexity: O((n+1)(k+1)) upper bound for memo states; each state has two transitions. Multiplicative implementations take min(k,n−k) factors; Pascal-recursive implementations instead memoize pairs of parameters.
spaceComplexity: O((n+1)(k+1)) memo storage and O(n) recursion. Python’s function-level cache persists across calls. Multiplicative variants store only a running result and loop index; Pascal variants retain memoized parameter pairs.
attribution: Unmodified reference from epi_judge_python_solutions/binomial_coefficients.py; Elements of Programming Interviews Judge contributors; CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 International, retained in repository LICENSE. Explanation authored for EPI Practice.
correctness: Partition k-subsets by whether they contain a fixed item. Excluding it yields C(n−1,k), including it yields C(n−1,k−1), and the cases are disjoint and exhaustive. Thus cached sums are exact by induction.
walkthrough: For C(5,2), combine C(4,2)=6 and C(4,1)=4 to obtain 10. Shared states such as C(3,1)=3 are computed once and reused. The walkthroughCase uses the judge’s JSON input format and expected observation.
edgeCases: Fixed-width result types require a representable binomial coefficient.
